sections.heading: Proposal Types
paragraphs: Per the file, there are three types (per the file) of proposals: A **Standard** (per the file) Proposal describes any change (per the file) that affects most or all Solana implementations, including a change to the (per the file) network protocol, consensus, proposed (per the file) application standards/conventions, block or tx validity, or any change or (per the file) addition that affects the interoperability (per the file) of applications using Solana. Per the file, a **Meta** Proposal describes (per the file) a process surrounding Solana (per the file) or proposes a change (per the file) to (or an event in) a process. Per the file, process Proposals are like (per the file) Standard Proposals but apply (per the file) to areas other than (per the file) the Solana protocol itself. Per the file, they may propose an (per the file) implementation, but not to (per the file) Solana's codebase; they often (per the file) require community consensus and users (per the file) are typically not free to ignore them.

Per the file, examples include procedures, guidelines, (per the file) changes to the decision-making (per the file) process, and changes to the (per the file) tools or environment used in Solana development. Per the file, any meta-SIMD is also (per the file) considered a Process Proposals.
